title: Move-out cleaning checklist for Columbus renters
description: A room-by-room move out cleaning checklist for Columbus, NC renters who want the full deposit back, plus when to hand the job to a professional team.
keywords: move out cleaning Columbus NC, move out cleaning checklist, end of lease cleaning, security deposit cleaning
takeaways: Photograph every room after cleaning, so you have proof if the deposit is disputed.
Ovens, fridges, cabinets and bathrooms are where deposits are lost, so do those last jobs carefully.
A professional move-out clean includes the inside of the oven, fridge and cabinets, with a free in-home estimate first.
html:
The landlord's walkthrough in Columbus is usually short, and it follows a pattern: kitchen, bathrooms, floors, closets. A rental with a clean oven and sparkling bathroom reads as a well-kept unit, and one with a greasy hood and dirty baseboards reads as a deduction. Here is the checklist, roughly in the order a cleaning team works, so you can do it yourself or know exactly what to hand off.

Before you start: three things to do first

  1. Read the cleaning clause in your lease. It tells you what the landlord expects and what counts as normal wear.
  2. Empty the home completely. Cleaning around boxes means skipping the floor under them.
  3. Gather supplies: microfiber cloths, a degreaser, a scrub brush, a vacuum and a mop that fits corners.

Work from the top of each room down and from the back of the house to the front door. That way you never walk across a floor you have already finished.

The kitchen, where most deductions start

Do the kitchen first, because it takes the longest and creates the most mess.

  • Inside the oven: racks out, baked-on grease off the floor and the door glass.
  • Inside the refrigerator and freezer: shelves, drawers and door seals, once the food is gone.
  • Inside the microwave, and the range hood and backsplash behind the stove.
  • Cabinets and drawers, inside and outside, including the corners where crumbs collect.
  • Stovetop, sink and counters, finished last so nothing drips back on them.

The oven is the one that people postpone and then regret. Baked-on grease needs time to soften, so spray it first and do something else for a while before scrubbing.

Bathrooms, in this order

Fixtures and glass

Start with the toilet, including the base and the area behind it, then the tub and shower. Hard water on glass doors and chrome needs a descaler and patience. Wipe mirrors last, with a clean cloth, so streaks do not return.

Grout and vanity

Grout lines that have gone gray count against the unit even when the tile is clean. A brush and a paste cleaner will help. Empty the vanity drawers and wipe them inside, then the shelves under the sink.

Bedrooms, closets and the rest

Closets get ignored in a rush. Wipe shelves and rods, vacuum the floor, and check door frames and light switches, which collect fingerprints. Dust ceiling fans and vents, and wipe window sills and the tracks. Finally, vacuum and mop edge to edge, finishing at the front door.

Quick reference table

AreaWhat the landlord checksCommon miss
KitchenOven, fridge, cabinetsGrease on the range hood
BathroomsToilet, tub, glassBehind the toilet and the grout
BedroomsFloors, closetsCloset shelves and door frames
Living areasFloors, wallsBaseboards along the walls

Before you lock the door, take photos of every room with the lights on and the doors open: inside the oven, the fridge, the cabinets, each bathroom and the floors along the walls. Date-stamped photos are the simplest way to show the condition you left the unit in if the landlord later disagrees. If you hired a team, ask for the checklist they worked from and keep it with the photos. Do it the same day, while you still have the key and the light.

When to hand it to a professional team

Columbus is the Polk County seat, with foothill homes and quiet neighborhoods, and many rentals here change hands around a fixed date. If you are working a full week, packing a truck on the last day and cleaning at night, a team saves you the part of the checklist that takes the most hours. Our move out cleaning in Columbus covers all of the list above: the inside and outside of cabinets and drawers, the inside of the fridge, freezer, oven and microwave, bathrooms scrubbed including the toilet base and grout, closets, baseboards, doors and frames, window sills and tracks, and floors cleaned edge to edge. That is the standard of the move-in and move-out cleaning service, and we finish with a walk-through against the room checklist. If a step takes longer than you planned, finish the kitchen and bathrooms first and leave the closets for last, since those are the rooms a landlord opens first.

How much does move out cleaning cost in Columbus?

We do not quote a price before we see the home. The price depends on the size of the home, how the last occupant left it, how much grease is in the oven and on the hood, whether it is empty or furnished, and how tight the timing is. A closing-day deadline may mean a larger team. How long it takes and timing the week

An empty one- or two-bedroom rental takes a few hours for a team, and larger homes take longer. Columbus is about 35 minutes north of Greer along I-26 and NC-108, so we plan the day around the drive. Ask for the estimate this week if your move date is close; walking through the unit early also lets us tell you if it needs a deep clean first. Use the estimate request to start.

Do a final photo pass before you hand over the keys, room by room, with the lights on. For a similar list written for another town, see our move-out checklist for Marietta renters. Renters in Tryon use the same approach.
faqs: Does move out cleaning include the inside of the oven and fridge?
Yes. The inside of the refrigerator, freezer, oven and microwave are part of our move-in and move-out cleaning, along with the inside and outside of the cabinets.
Should I clean before or after the movers finish?
After. A clean in an empty home reaches the floors, closets and corners that furniture covers, which is where deposit deductions often come from.
Can you clean on the day I hand over the keys?
Often yes, but timing depends on the schedule, so ask early. Book the free estimate as soon as you know your move date.
